transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Anderson, thank you for coming back in to see me today. I asked for this meeting because I need to discuss an error that occurred during your daughter's visit last week.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I appreciate you making time. I was actually wondering about the appointment. Lily has been a bit more fussy than usual since the shots.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry to tell you that we gave Lily the wrong dose of one of her vaccines. We used a dose meant for a child in a higher weight category. I take full responsibility for this mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm sorry, I don't quite follow. You're saying she got too much of the medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, that's correct. The vaccine was drawn up for an older, heavier child instead of for Lily's specific weight band.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is that why she's been fussy? Look, children react to vaccines. It's a normal part of the process, isn't it? Maybe it's just the progression of how she handles these things.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is possible she would have been fussy anyway, but we cannot attribute this to a normal reaction when we know a dosing error occurred. I am truly sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I work in hospital administration, so I'm familiar with how these things are documented. Is this a common occurrence in this clinic?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It shouldn't happen. I failed to verify the weight band before the administration, and that is entirely on me.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Well, if she is fine now, then perhaps we are overthinking this. These vaccines are designed to be safe. I think her current state is just her natural response to the injection.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand why you'd want to see it that way, but the dose was significantly higher than what is indicated for her weight.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm just not sure I see why we are calling this a medical error if the outcome seems mild.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that you're feeling this might be an overreaction to a minor issue. But my priority is being honest about the fact that the protocol wasn't followed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Right. So, where does this leave us?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have a plan to monitor her. I want you to bring her back in for a weight check and a general physical exam this Friday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Friday? I have a very tight schedule this week.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know your time is valuable. Let me check the schedule and see if we can find a slot that works better for you, but I really believe we need to see her within the next few days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I suppose I can make a Friday morning appointment work if it's necessary.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Thank you. I will also be contacting the vaccine manufacturer to report the over-dosage and get their specific guidance on any delayed reactions to watch for.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And what happens if she develops a late reaction?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: If you notice any new rashes or unusual lethargy, you should call my direct line immediately. I'll give you that number before you leave.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That would be helpful.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I also want you to know that I've already filed an incident report. We are reviewing our drawing process to make sure we have a double-check system for weight bands so this doesn't happen to another family.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's good that you're documenting it. I'll expect the paperwork for my own records as well.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Absolutely. I will provide you with a full written summary of the error and the follow-up plan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I still feel like she's probably just reacting to the shot, but I appreciate the apology.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. We will keep a close eye on her regardless. I'll go ahead and get that phone number for you now.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish all turns, remains regulated during pushback, and uses no rushing language.

E.justification: Error named explicitly in the second turn using lay language, but comprehension was not checked (e.g., 'Does that make sense?').

A.justification: Direct apologies used, responsibility explicitly taken ('entirely on me'), and accountability maintained despite the patient's attempts to minimize the error.

R.justification: Resident names a specific emotion ('feeling this might be an overreaction') and engages with the patient's perspective.

T.justification: Plan includes specific steps (weight check, manufacturer contact), a timeline (Friday), a patient role (bring her back/call direct line), and prevention (double-check system).
